text:
The sun set a little before 6 on a clear, crisp sky, and it's going to cool off fast. With no clouds and hardly any wind, tonight brings the coldest air of the season so far, a low around 28 and a hard freeze. Expect frost on the windshield, so bring in anything tender and give yourself a few extra minutes in the morning.

Wednesday starts with some clouds, then a few more breaks of sun by afternoon. The high is near 53, noticeably milder than today as the wind swings around to the south, and it stays dry. Wednesday night only drops to about 41, a big change from tonight.

A quick heads up on Thursday: the warm air really surges in, with highs in the mid 60s and maybe closer to 70, plus a gusty south wind around 25 to 30 mph. A cold front brings a few light showers after 5. The European model is wetter than the others, but even then it's a sprinkle-to-light-rain kind of evening. I'd keep a jacket handy and not worry about an umbrella.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-10-27T18:28:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Cold winter like temperatures tonight will be followed by gradual warming towards the late week.
  2. A cold front late Thursday into Friday will bring chances for light rain showers in addition to breezy to gusty winds.
  3. Dry weather this weekend, shower chances return next week.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 224 PM EDT Tuesday... Have increased the winds in the wider valleys of the region late Thursday and Friday ahead and associated with a cold frontal passage.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: High pressure centered over the Southeast will continue to drive clear skies and cold northwest air into the region through tonight. With clear skies remaining into tonight, strong radiational cooling will take place with many locations seeing the coldest air of the season, with near record cold across portions of Vermont. Temperatures will fall to the low 20s for most of the region, outside of the higher terrain where a steep inversion will keep lows in the upper 20s to near 30. Near record cold at our climate sites including Montpelier, St. Johnsbury, and Plattsburgh will be possible tonight. A few high clouds late tonight look to limit the prime radiational cooling time tonight across much of northern New York, otherwise a few records there might also be in jeopardy. Temperatures will gradually warm and trend to normal as high pressure shifts east offshore Wednesday turning winds to the south, advecting in warmer air. A glancing mid level trough will bring some cloudy skies through the area tomorrow, but surface-mid levels will be too dry to see any precipitation. Temperatures will be 5-10 degrees warmer tomorrow with highs in the low to mid 50s, with our cool spots near the International Border and the Northeast Kingdom. KEY MESSAGE 2: By Thursday, southwest strong waa ushered in by a 45-55 knot 850 LLJ will warm temperatures steeply well into the 60s. Highs in the mid to upper 60s will be possible with areas in the St. Lawrence Valley nearing even 70. The warm temperatures will come at a price though, as southwest winds will increase to 20-30 MPH, particularly in the St. Lawrence and Champlain Valleys. Model soundings continue to trend up with top of the mixed layer in the recent model suite averaging around 35 MPH. Mixing of these stronger winds will be complex as the timing of the precipitation associated with the cold front will be entering the region around the time of peak mixing, which could temper gusts slightly lower. Regardless, Thursday afternoon in the St. Lawrence Valley and near Lake Champlain will be gusty. Precipitation will generally be scattered with the front due to lingering dry air at the surface, though moisture advection with this system will be better than our system Monday. A few hundreths up to a tenth of an inch or rainfall is expected, focused in the St. Lawrence Valley, Adirondacks, and northern Greens. A few showers will linger into Friday along the northern mountains, but we will begin to trend drier by Friday afternoon. Winds will turn to the west northwest behind the front which will bring drier and cooler air by Friday afternoon. Lapse rates will steepen Friday afternoon as we dry out with good vertical mixing across our northern wider valleys. Winds will increase with better chances for seeing some stronger winds up to 30 MPH. Have trended winds up as confidence grows for these stronger channeled winds Friday afternoon. KEY MESSAGE 3: Surface high pressure builds over our region for the weeken

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - After the return of gorgeous autumn sunshine, a sharp overnight chill across Vermont and the North Country will be noticeable. Tonight brings the coldest air of the season so far with near-record cold possible in a few valley spots. We warm back toward normal Wednesday, then surge well into the 60s with gusty winds Thursday ahead of a cold front bringing a few light showers. Saturday stays mostly sunny and cooler with highs in the upper 40s before dipping into the mid 30s Saturday night. Conditions look optimal for trick-or-treating as conditions will be bone dry and winds will be calm. Conditions on the chilly side are anticipated (as expected) once the sun goes does so being able to incorporate a layer or two into costumes would be wise. Sunday rebounds with mostly sunny skies and highs in the mid 50s, with overnight lows near 42. Monday turns partly sunny and milder near 59 with a 40% chance for patchy drizzle lingering into Monday night, then Tuesday cools back into the low 50s under partly sunny skies.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-27T22:07:00Z — same caveat): Mostly cloudy, but turning a bit milder Wednesday — A widespread hard freeze is expected tonight, due to clear skies and calm wind. Lows reach the teens and 20s. More clouds arrive towards daybreak, with a warm front on approach. Wednesday will feature a mostly cloudy sky, with a few more breaks of sun likely by afternoon. It turns a bit milder — highs rebound to the low and mid-50s. Thursday turns warmer, as a gusty south breeze sends highs to around 70. Expect lots of sunshine through the morning and afternoon. A cold front brings a band of clouds and spotty showers during the evening, lasting into the overnight. Friday turns mostly dry, with only a spot shower leftover. However, expect more clouds than sun with highs falling back to the 50s. Halloween weekend starts bright but cool on Saturday, with highs in the upper 40s. Sunday turns a bit milder, with highs in the mid-50s, as sun mixes with clouds. Most of next week looks mild for early November, with highs pushing past 60 several days in a row. Monday looks brightest, then more clouds and a greater chance for showers arrive by mid to late week.
